title: Paquimé (Casas Grandes)
summary: Paquimé is an adobe settlement in the municipality of Casas Grandes, Chihuahua, at the foot of the Sierra Madre Occidental. UNESCO dates its development to 700-1475, with its height in the 14th and 15th centuries. It linked the Pueblo world to the north with Mesoamerica; EBSCO says it was abandoned around 1450.

uncertainty.note: UNESCO gives development 700-1475 with apogee in the 14th-15th centuries; EBSCO gives settlement from the twelfth century and abandonment around 1450. Sources differ; span follows UNESCO.

importance.justification: UNESCO calls it the largest archaeological zone representing the peoples of the Chihuahua Desert and a hub of trade between the Pueblo world and Mesoamerica.
